searchText: This is a bit unorthodox, but curious what client teams think of considering https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/deprecate-selfdestruct/11907 for Shanghai. **To be clear, the EIP is only _saying_ we intend to deprecate SELFDESTRUCT, it's not a code change**. But, by marking SELFDESTRUCT as "officially" deprecated, it might help reduce reliance on it. Happy to put it on the agenda for the next ACDE call if people think it's worth considering 🙂 EIP Link: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6049 Generally in favor of it, but what is the EL impact? It's not like we would log a warning message at contract execution whenever we execute a `SELFDESTRUCT`. This feels like it is more of a message to the dApp developers and tooling like solidity should spit out the compiler warnings. No EL impact. This is basically just a signal to the broader community. Perhaps code deployment should sniff and warn too. You could remove it from the solidity compiler, or at least add a warning Interesting option... there's always older compilers if you absolutely need it. and raw assembly Right, and Solidity (or Vyper) could choose to first add an error message, and eventually block deployements Compiler complaining, compiler dropping support for the opcode (outside of assembly), etherscan warning on transactions to contracts with self destruct opcode in them, wallets warning on such transactions, etc. Step 1 to all of this is a clear signal from the core devs that SELFDESTRUCT is deprecated and will eventually be removed. Will eventually be removed or changed I'm not a fan of setting the precedent of removing opcodes no longer considered useful, unless there is an extremely good argument that it won't be considered a precedent in the future. Especially if there happens to be a proposal that doesn't break things (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6190)

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content:
This is a bit unorthodox, but curious what client teams think of considering https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/deprecate-selfdestruct/11907 for Shanghai. **To be clear, the EIP is only _saying_ we intend to deprecate SELFDESTRUCT, it's not a code change**.

 But, by marking SELFDESTRUCT as "officially" deprecated, it might help reduce reliance on it. Happy to put it on the agenda for the next ACDE call if people think it's worth considering 🙂

This feels like it is more of a message to the dApp developers and tooling like solidity should spit out the compiler warnings.
